sections.title: The Healing of the Lame Man
observations: In this section, we see Peter and John going to the temple at the hour of prayer. They encounter a man who was lame from birth, begging at the temple gate. This moment is significant as it highlights the early church's commitment to prayer and worship.

Peter's response to the lame man is profound. Instead of giving him money, he offers healing in the name of Jesus Christ. This act demonstrates the power of faith and the authority of Jesus, emphasizing that true healing comes from Him.

The healing itself is a miraculous sign that points to the reality of Jesus' resurrection and His ongoing work through the apostles. It serves as a testimony to the power of the Gospel and the compassion of Christ.

sections.title: Peter's Address to the People
observations: After the healing, a crowd gathers, astonished by what has happened. Peter seizes this opportunity to preach the Gospel, addressing the people directly and pointing them to Jesus as the source of the miracle.
He emphasizes that it was not by their own power or piety that the man was healed, but by faith in Jesus' name. This underscores the theme of reliance on Christ rather than human effort or merit.

Peter calls the people to repentance, urging them to turn away from their sins and to embrace the salvation offered through Jesus. This is a key moment in the early church's mission to spread the Gospel.

importantVerses.commentary: Peter said, 'Silver and gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, rise up and walk!' This verse highlights the power of Jesus' name and the priority of spiritual over material wealth.
Repent therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out. This verse emphasizes the necessity of repentance in the Christian faith and the promise of forgiveness.

questions: What does the healing of the lame man teach us about the nature of faith and the power of Jesus' name?
How does Peter's sermon reflect the early church's understanding of Jesus' role as the Messiah?
In what ways can we apply Peter's call to repentance in our own lives and communities?
